messages:
alex: Hi team — hitting a weird 400 from the embeddings endpoint after this morning's client bump. Error: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 0". I think payload shape is wrong but not sure why.

alex: here's the failing payload we logged (trimmed):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "input": [["user text 1"], ["user text 2"]]
}
```

maya: thanks, can you paste the exact request_id from the response headers (x-request-id) and the full error body? also which SDK/runtime?

alex: no request_id in logs (400 returned before we logged headers). Using our in-house tiny wrapper around the JS SDK — but we call embedBatch(items) where items is already an array. suspect double-wrapping somewhere.

oliver: that payload shows double-wrapped arrays. embeddings endpoint expects either a single string or a flat array of strings: "input": "single doc" or "input": ["doc1","doc2"]. When you send [[...]] the service treats the inner arrays as non-text input -> parser yields empty vectors -> dimension mismatch.

oliver: quick repro curl to see the same error: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":[["foo"]]}'
```

rachel: FYI we pushed a minor change in our internal client yesterday that automatically wraps single-string inputs into an array. If your wrapper also wraps arrays again you get [[...]] — classic double-wrap.

maya: two asks: 1) can you paste the minimal JS snippet that calls the SDK so we can reproduce locally? 2) any temporary workaround?

alex: minimal repro (our wrapper):
```js
function embedBatch(items) {
  // legacy code: ensure array
  const payloadItems = Array.isArray(items) ? [items] : [items]; // <-- bug, wraps arrays
  return client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood-embed-1', input: payloadItems });
}
// calling with an array: embedBatch(["a","b"]) // results in [["a","b"]]
```

oliver: yep that's it. Quick fix: change to `const payloadItems = Array.isArray(items) ? items : [items];` so you don't nest.

oliver: Also note: large nested arrays can trigger batching/throughput code paths that assume flat lists and may cause increased latency or partial failures. If you are sending huge single requests, try chunking to 128-512 inputs per request.

alex: patched our wrapper and verified — now getting 200 + embeddings, vectors length 1536. Thanks.

rachel: we'll add a guard in the SDK to normalize input shapes and emit a clearer error message if shape is nested. Filed ENG-ML ticket EN-3421.

eng-support-bot: This thread has been escalated to #eng-ml and linked to EN-3421. If you want a hotfix in the public SDK, please add a short repro gist and label it "high-priority".

alex: adding repro gist now. one more question — will customers see any billing anomalies when they accidentally send nested arrays?

oliver: good question — currently we reject invalid payloads early (400) so they won't be charged for tokenized outputs, but malformed requests that still parse can cause chargeable work. Best practice: validate on client and limit batch sizes. We'll add a note to the docs and the SDK error.

alex: perfect, thanks everyone. marking resolved on our side. :thumbsup:
